lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 33

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Price of Retention
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scratching did not return.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Something else answered in its place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From inside BAH-lahg's pack the fourth knock still hung in the air, unanswered. No one moved to open the straps. BAH-lahg had gone still in the particular way he did when the ground itself had become untrustworthy. en-HEH-doo watched the canvas without reaching for it, the figurine turning once in her fingers and then forgotten. Ninsun stood two feet from them, hands clenched white at her sides, and neither of the others looked at her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They were not looking through her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They were looking past her entirely, the way a person's eyes slide off a shadow that has not quite decided whether it wants to be noticed.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We need to move,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg said. He stood and slung the pack over one shoulder. The leather straps groaned under the weight of whatever still moved inside it.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Zeek? You coming, or are you going to keep staring at your book?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked from BAH-lahg to Ninsun.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She was visibly terrified and just as visibly refusing to stop existing because the world around her had decided she was an inconvenience to be filed away.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Zeek,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she whispered. Her voice hitched on his name.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: They don't hear me. It's like I'm not even making sound.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He took a slow breath. His hand drifted to the journal, then past it. He had told himself he would not bargain with the City again. He knew exactly what it cost—the holes it punched cleanly through history, the strange smooth empty spaces that remained afterward like scars with nothing underneath them. The worst part had never been the clean forgetting. It was knowing that something important had been taken and having no shape left behind to mourn.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Looking at Ninsun changed the arithmetic.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The shadows in the room seemed to curl toward her. The stone behind her had begun to soften at the edges, the way limestone softened when the ledger was preparing to close an account.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He spoke without raising his voice.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Her name is Ninsun. She is with us. She stays.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For a moment nothing answered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then BAH-lahg blinked, once, hard, as if something behind his eyes had been forcibly rethreaded. He looked at Ninsun with the startled recognition of a man who has just remembered a debt he did not know he owed.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Ninsun,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said. The name arrived incomplete, as though retrieved from a damaged tablet.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Right. The scholar.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo's gaze slid toward her and held. Not with warmth. With the remote attention she now gave anything that had been declared relevant by someone else.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun exhaled a sound that was almost a sob and almost nothing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek felt the cost arrive a heartbeat later.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was not dramatic. A single clean absence opened somewhere behind his ribs—the specific reason he had decided she was worth the price. He still knew her name. He still knew she belonged with them. He still knew he had paid something irreversible to keep her present in the others' minds.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He simply could no longer remember what had made her worth that price in the first place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg shifted the pack on his shoulder. Whatever was inside it had gone quiet.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: What did you just do, Zeek? Why is she still here?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her, then at the wall of names behind them.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Because I decided she was.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He was not entirely sure, even as he said it, whether he believed his own answer.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They began walking. Ninsun stayed close enough behind him that he could hear the rhythm of her breathing. He knew her name. He knew she belonged with them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The rest was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them the chisel began again, unhurried and precise.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The City kept its records.
